mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% in the month preceding the forecast period reduces near-term discount rates, lowering the present value of future earnings and thereby depressing S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during pre-rates-increase periods (p > 0.05 in t-test).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly pay growth acceleration (PAYEMS) exceeding 0.5% above the prior month's rate signals stronger wage growth, which increases consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, pushing S&P 500 60-day forward returns positively.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly growth rate > 0.5% over prior month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no significant correlation with PAYEMS acceleration (Pearson IC < 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 105 suggests weakening manufacturing demand, which reduces corporate order backlogs and lowers 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during stable INDPRO periods (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL > 237.7) indicate persistent demand pressures, which, if unmitigated, raises expected future cost structures and dampens S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL remains above 237.7 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not negatively correlated with CPIAUCSL persistence (Pearson IC > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in unemployment (UNRATE below 4.5%) coinciding with a decline in reserve balances (not directly observable here) typically precedes rate cuts, which boost equity valuations and drive positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4.5% in the prior month
failure_condition: No significant positive return when UNRATE crosses below 4.5% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly rise in retail sales proxy (not available in catalog; using HOUST as a demand proxy) above 1020 signals resilient consumer demand, which elevates earnings expectations and supports positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST exceeds 1020 in the current month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no significant positive relationship with HOUST levels (IC < 0.15).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in housing starts (not directly observable; using HOUST as a proxy for economic activity) over three months indicates cooling activity, which reduces growth expectations and produces negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST declines for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower during multi-month HOUST declines (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged period of falling industrial production (INDPRO) below 106 suggests supply-side softness, lowering market confidence and resulting in negative 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not consistently negative during INDPRO < 106 episodes (p > 0.05).
